'No production changes' and 'no flag changes' reflect only the windows queried (144 minutes of change events, and the flag provider's recent history). A change outside those windows would not have been seen.

input.executive_summary:
For roughly six minutes late on 25 September 2026 (from 22:19 to 22:25 UTC, per the service metrics), the online shop's account page was very slow to load. Shoppers viewing their account and basket total saw page loads that took well over a second instead of being near-instant, and a small additional share of those page loads failed outright — mostly because shoppers gave up and closed the connection while waiting. Ordering and browsing elsewhere on the site were not reported as affected.

The cause was not in the shop itself but in an internal service, owned by the same organisation, that calculates basket totals; it began responding slowly to nearly every request. The automated on-call system picked up the alert, traced the slowdown to that internal service within about fifteen seconds, and restarted it. The shop returned to its normal speed immediately afterwards and the incident was closed as mitigated. A draft code change has since been proposed for follow-up review.
input.root_cause: io-shop's account page calls pricing.io-internal.svc (io-pricing) to render basket-total; from 22:19:00Z that call started taking roughly 1.5s on essentially every request, and io-shop's synchronous dependence on it pushed p50/p95/p99 up by more than an order of magnitude. No deploy, release, or feature-flag change was found on io-shop or in the change window, so the trigger was a degradation inside io-pricing itself; restarting io-pricing cleared it, which points at process-local state (e.g. pool/GC/thread exhaustion) rather than anything in io-shop's code.
